text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient is a 25-year-old female involved in a rear-end collision with immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin. Given the mechanism of injury and the location of the severe pain, I need to assess for potential hip dislocation or femoral neck fracture; have you been able to move your right hip or knee at all, and is the right leg visibly deformed or shortened?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Posterior Hip Dislocation. The clinical presentation of severe groin pain combined with a right leg that is shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated following high-energy trauma is pathognomonic for this injury. REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Hip_XRay_series.
